 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On The 13th Of August, 2024
Misc. Criminal Case No. 33533 of 2024

Sanju @ Sanju Urveti (Ureti)
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Ms. Gayatri Ladhiya - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri K.S. Baghel - Ga for the respondent/State.
 Order

This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with Crime No. 144/2024 registered at Police Station- Adhartal, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 376 (D) of IPC.
2.
As per prosecution story, the allegation against the present applicant is of committing rape upon the prosecutrix.
On the basis of aforesaid, FIR was registered.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
FIR has been lodged after six months.
There is no proper explanation of delay in lodging the FIR.
MLC report also does not support the prosecution story.
There was disputed between prosecutrix and co-accused Vijay regarding money transaction.
Applicant is friend of co-accused Vijay therefore, prosecutrix has falsely implicated him.

In view of the aforesaid, prayer has been made to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that present applicant and co- accused have committed gang rape with the prosecutrix who is partially paralyzed.

Present applicant is absconding and a reward has been announced for his arrest as well as permanent arrest has also been issued against him.
5.

Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to seriousness of offence as well as allegation levelled against the applicant, I am not inclined to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.
